about.paragraph2: Along the way I've led engineering work at Reforge and built products at TherapyZen and Better Health Therapeutics. That work taught me how to create responsive user interfaces, integrate APIs cleanly, and keep backend systems secure and efficient, especially in healthcare, where reliability matters most.
about.paragraph3: I studied Statistics and Psychology at Rutgers University, and both still shape how I build: I care about the data behind a product and the people who use it. I'm passionate about AI-powered platforms that make digital workflows faster, smarter and more useful.

mbti.title: Adaptive MBTI Personality Quiz Engine
mbti.tagline: An adaptive personality assessment application built around a modular Bayesian inference engine.
description: Rather than presenting every question in a fixed sequence, the engine uses previous responses to estimate personality traits and select the next question based on how much uncertainty it is expected to reduce.

The system separates the core assessment logic from the user interface, with distinct components for question selection, probabilistic updates, personality classification, and API integration. This separation makes the engine easier to test, extend, and evaluate independently of the quiz experience.

A key engineering challenge is balancing assessment efficiency with classification accuracy. The engine updates its estimates after each answer, evaluates the remaining uncertainty across four MBTI dimensions, and determines when there is enough confidence to conclude the assessment. Simulation and benchmarking tools help compare adaptive question selection with alternative strategies.
The result is a more efficient, data-driven quiz experience supported by a reusable assessment architecture, a Python backend, and a browser-based interface.

networkLab.title: Azure Network Infrastructure Lab (Under development)
networkLab.tagline: A teaching project prepared for Network Infrastructure Management students.
networkLab.description: An Infrastructure as Code lab created as a teaching example for Network Infrastructure Management students. The project deploys an Azure Resource Group, a Virtual Network, three network segments, Network Security Groups, Windows Server virtual machines, and an Ubuntu virtual machine prepared for security monitoring with Wazuh. It demonstrates network segmentation, restricted backend access, and repeatable environment provisioning with Terraform.
